text:
alex: Heads up — after flipping the kernel_selector experiment for Mixtral-8x on prod (auto -> 'prefer_fast'), we saw a consistent perf win but a surprising drop in our regression eval for the summarization suite. 8ms/token -> 5.5ms/token, but Rouge-L down ~4.5pts on the nightly run. :confused:
priya: ugh. can you paste the experiment id and the runtime config? any other toggles (quant/rope) in that rollout?
alex: experiment id exp-mx-kselect-2026-03-17, rollout to 20% traffic. Runtime config snippet from the deploy agent:
```json
{"model":"mixtral-8x","kernel_selector":"prefer_fast","kernel_priority":["tiled_attn","fast_kv","fallback"],"rope_scale":1.0,"quant":"auto"}
```
marco: "quant":"auto" is a red flag — auto can pick int8 path for some kernels. perf-bot alert?
perf-bot: [automated] RegressionDetector: summary_suite: rouge_l -4.5, pass_rate 62% -> 48% (p<0.01). Linked eval: https://ci.internal/evals/4821
jenn: I reran the eval locally pinned to the same model weights but forced old kernel ordering and quant=off — scores match baseline. so it's runtime-only.
priya: good catch. alex — can we get a perf profile (flamegraph) and the kv-cache hit/miss rates around long-context tests? my hypothesis: fast kernel trades precision for slightly different k/v layout that punishes RoPE edge cases.
alex: attaching the flame summary (excerpt):
```
CPU: mixtral_forward
- tiled_attn_kernel (avg 2.1ms)
- kv_cache_read (avg 0.4ms, miss 12%)
- fast_kv_transform (avg 1.3ms)
- quant_dequant (avg 0.2ms when active)
```
And kv cache misses spike on sequences with repeated long prefixes; eviction count +42% on canary.
marco: that eviction spike might change position ids observed by attention if our cache refill path isn't atomic between tiled_attn and fast_kv. race window could manifest in different effective RoPE offsets.
jenn: interesting — especially because mixtral's head dim packing is sensitive to kernel tiling. Did the selector pick a slightly different kernel for heads with odd dims?
alex: yes, selector chose tiled_attn for heads % 4 != 0 and fast_kv for the rest. That partitioning wasn't present in baseline.
priya: @alex can you try forcing kernel_priority to exact baseline ordering and re-run Canary at 5% before full rollback? we need to know if kernel swap alone reproduces the drop.
alex: started a canary with kernel_priority=["fallback","tiled_attn"] and quant=off. kicked off eval run.
perf-bot: [automated] Canary run started: canary-181234-c1 (5% traffic). ETA 12m.
ops-bot: FYI — I muted alerts on exp-mx-kselect-2026-03-17 to reduce noise during investigation. remember to re-enable after decision.
marco: parallel hypothesis: rope_scale was left at 1.0, but the fast_kv kernel applies a tiny per-head scaling to avoid overflow, which effectively changes numeric behavior. need to diff attention outputs at layer granularity. can someone run a deterministic forward on a failing sample and diff activations?
jenn: I'll take that. running with debug dumps on the failing sample id=svc-99321. will upload diffs to the eval link.
alex: quick interim: we've paused the rollout to 20% (stopped new traffic). current plan: 1) rollback kernel_selector for Mixtral to baseline ordering 2) pin quant=off in runtime config 3) collect activation diffs and kv trace 4) if diffs localize to fast_kv numeric path, open kernel bug with runtime.
priya: +1. also add a targeted unit-eval that exercises long-prefix repetitive contexts so this doesn't regress again silently. I'll own the test.
alex: noted. created ticket INF-1729 with those steps and linked canary logs. assigning to marco for kernel-level analysis, jenn for activation diffs, and me for rollout/rollback ops.
marco: preliminary diffs show sub-1e-3 differences in attention logits at layer 9 that amplify downstream. looks like a quantized multiply path is using fused accumulate -> fp16 cast earlier. filing low-level kernel issue.
jenn: uploaded diffs and a small repro that reproduces the rouge drop in under 30 steps. see https://ci.internal/repros/99321
perf-bot: [automated] Canary eval finished: rouge_l delta -0.2 (canary pinned) — suggests quant toggle was the main contributor.
alex: ok that's actionable. rollback done: kernel_selector set back, quant forced off globally for Mixtral. we'll monitor nightly eval; re-open experiment only after kernel fixes and adding the long-prefix unit test.
priya: thanks team. small note: add a check in the selector to avoid per-head kernel partitioning for models with non-uniform head dims — that guard would have prevented this.
marco: will prototype a selector rule: if head_dim % tile != 0 -> prefer fallback. putting up a PR.
jen n: :thumbsup: 
alex: closing thread for now. will post follow-ups after kernel PR and nightly green. thanks everyone.
